claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-count leukaemia puts children at risk of serious complications or death** from leukostasis/hyperviscosity. Hyperleukocytosis should prompt consideration of acute leukaemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Leukostasis** (symptomatic hyperleukocytosis) is diagnosed clinically: CNS abnormalities, respiratory distress or other organ dysfunction put down to hyperleukocytosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Complications:** ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke · thrombosis and infarction in the lungs or kidneys · DIC · tumour lysis syndrome. Their frequency depends on the type of leukaemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The main risks are bleeding or thrombosis, most often in the brain and lung.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ask about** visual disturbance, dizziness, tinnitus, behaviour change and altered consciousness. **Look for** altered mental status, ataxia, papilloedema, retinal abnormalities, signs of raised intracranial pressure and increased work of breathing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult oncology early; arrange retrieval to a tertiary centre and consider PICU for all children with hyperleukocytosis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with oncology before further blood collection**, so time-sensitive investigations are prioritised.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods usually needed:** FBE and film · UEC · group and hold · LFT · CMP · LDH · coagulation screen with fibrinogen · uric acid · G6PD assay.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An adjusted coagulation tube may be needed if haematocrit is under 0.21** — discuss with the laboratory before taking blood.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CXR; consider neuroimaging if there are neurological symptoms or signs.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitoring:** continuous saturations (consider cardiac monitoring) · **4-hourly neuro obs** · **6-hourly FBE, UEC, uric acid, CMP** ± coagulation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start hyperhydration at 125 mL/m²/hr (or double maintenance) with no added potassium** — 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% dextrose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Platelet consumption can be extremely rapid; several platelet transfusions may be needed per day.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Correct coagulopathy: keep INR under 2.0, APTT under 80 and fibrinogen over 1.0.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid red cell transfusion unless oncology suggests it, and then limit it to 5–10 mL/kg** to minimise hyperviscosity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
